description: A column of words told to read as dates, which upstream labels rather than refuses. `formatType: "time"` decides the *grammar* before the scale gets a say, and it reaches further than the labels: `isFieldOrDatumDefForTimeFormat` is `formatType === 'time' || (!formatType && isTemporalFieldDef(...))`, so the column is **parsed** as well — Vega-Lite writes `toDate(datum["a"])` over it, `toDate` is `Date.parse` for anything that is not already a number or a date, and `Date.parse('one')` is `NaN` rather than nothing. Every row therefore carries the same NaN, the band collapses to a single entry, and the label is d3's arithmetic on an Invalid Date: every getter answers NaN, every NaN goes through the same padding, and the multi-format falls all the way through to `%Y` because `second(date) < date` is false rather than true. `0NaN` — three characters padded to four. The first row is that, unformatted; the second names a format, so the same NaN is written through `%b %d, %Y` and comes out ` NaN, 0NaN`, a name field contributing nothing where a number field says NaN. The third must not move: real dates, the same format, read the way they read anywhere. Three things here were wrong and each is one character wide, which is the point — the labels are turned on their side, so a label's *width* is the chart's height and the corpus differed by eight pixels nobody could account for. The fourth panel is what makes the *parse* visible rather than only its labels: a text mark over the same column, as a plain category. A nominal text channel writes `isValid(datum["a"]) ? datum["a"] : "" + datum["a"]`, and `isValid` is false of a NaN exactly as it is of a null — so the second arm runs either way and prints the two apart, `NaN` against `null`. Without it every mutant of `toDate` survives, because a label coerces both to the same Invalid Date and the chart is otherwise the same size. The **empty string** is the one input `toDate` refuses outright — `_ == null || _ === '' ? null : parser(_)`, two guards and only these two — and it is pinned by `ToDateTest` rather than here, because a row carrying one puts a *null* into a stack and upstream keys a stack's groups by `JSON.stringify`, under which a NaN and a null are the same group. That is a separate divergence with a separate cause and it is recorded as its own task; a fixture carrying it would fail for a reason that has nothing to do with dates.
